component: core.session_env, cli._specs_resolution, context bind, Codex sandbox process ancestry
expected: A successful context bind in Codex must be visible to all resolver-driven dadaia CLI commands in that same Codex thread. Commands such as bugs status, bugs append, specs doctor, memory commands, and related specs-dir consumers should resolve repos/<bound-context>/specs without requiring --specs-dir or legacy eval exports.
notes: Root cause: dadaia only treats CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and CODEX_SESSION_ID as harness-native session ids, but current Codex tool subprocesses expose CODEX_THREAD_ID. Because context bind does not persist a session record keyed by CODEX_THREAD_ID and Codex sandboxing collapses the CLI ancestry channel to pid 1, the fallback bind-epoch attribution cannot recover the context. This affects Codex users broadly and blocks the mandatory bug-registration path unless --specs-dir is supplied explicitly. Paths and machine-local details redacted.
repro: In a trusted Codex interactive workspace session: 1. Run .dadaia/.venv/bin/dadaia context bind dadaia-workspace. 2. Run .dadaia/.venv/bin/dadaia bugs status with no --specs-dir. 3. Observe the command fails to resolve specs_dir even though the bind confirmation succeeded. Diagnostic evidence: tool command env has CODEX_THREAD_ID set, CODEX_SESSION_ID absent; process ancestry visible to the CLI inside the Codex sandbox is only [1].
surface: Codex Layer-1 context bind and resolver-driven dadaia CLI commands
symptom: Inside an interactive Codex session, after running dadaia context bind dadaia-workspace successfully, resolver-driven commands such as dadaia bugs status still fail with: Could not resolve specs_dir. The same session receives context memory injection, but CLI commands do not see the bound context.
title: Codex bound context is invisible to dadaia CLI commands

expected: specs/backlog/remote-bugs/*.md and specs/backlog/remote-bugs/_archive/*.md should be explicitly opted in, matching the PM-curated backlog truth contract.
notes: Impact: critical triage notes can be left on disk but omitted from commits/releases, making remote bug intake unreliable.
repro: Create specs/backlog/remote-bugs/<new>.md, then run git status --short --untracked-files=all and git check-ignore -v for that path. The path is ignored by .gitignore rule /specs/backlog/*.
symptom: New Markdown reports under specs/backlog/remote-bugs are ignored by the repository .gitignore even though the workspace uses that directory for active remote bug intake. Existing files are tracked only because they were already in the index; new reports are invisible to normal git status unless force-added.
title: remote-bugs backlog intake is ignored by gitignore
